chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, he said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed three or two rakʿahs. He said: He builds upon the lesser amount and takes what is certain, and after finishing he recites a light tashahhud, likewise from the beginning of the salat (prayer) and its end. The correct way to understand this report is that he only builds upon the lesser amount when his conjecture inclines toward it, and he prays its completion as a recommended act. But when the conjecture is balanced, then building upon the greater amount is more precautionary, when he completes after finishing the salat (prayer) as we have explained. And that which confirms this is...

key_terms.أَحْوَطُ: more precautionary; safer in legal practice
key_terms.اعْتِدَالِ الْوَهْمِ: the balancing of conjecture; when neither side of the doubt outweighs the other
key_terms.الْبِنَاءُ عَلَى الْأَكْثَرِ: building upon the greater amount; taking the higher number as the basis
key_terms.تَشَهُّدًا خَفِيفًا: a light tashahhud; a brief testimony recited after completion
key_terms.لَا يَدْرِي: he does not know; indicating uncertainty in the number of rakʿahs
key_terms.وَهْمُهُ: his supposition or impression; the side toward which uncertainty inclines
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ بِالْجَزْمِ: he takes what is certain; acting on what is firmly known
key_terms.يَبْنِي عَلَى النُّقْصَانِ: he builds upon the lesser amount; treating the lower number as the basis

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if he doubts whether he prayed two rakʿahs or three?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for doubt in the number of rakʿahs in salat (prayer), specifically whether one has prayed two or three. It explains that one may build on the lesser amount when one's supposition inclines that way, but if the doubt is evenly balanced, then building on the greater amount with post-prayer completion is more precautionary.
